India is the higher-scoring country of the two, by 5.8 runs

A first innings averages 166.0 at the 7 India grounds we hold ball-by-ball data for, across 488 matches, against 160.2 in Australia over 478 matches. Scoring rates run 7.95 an over against 7.61. Of the countries we track, Pakistan is the highest at 172.4 and West Indies the lowest at 149.3.

Chasing costs 15.9 runs on average in Australia and 14.0 in India — but the country average hides the spread that matters. It is 19.0 at Sydney Cricket Ground and 13.2 at Melbourne Cricket Ground. A total that defends comfortably at one ground is chased down at another.

How the live prediction works

It starts when the match does. There is no pre-match tip here. Win probability is recalculated after every ball from the score, wickets in hand, balls and runs remaining, and how the pitch is behaving in this innings rather than on average.

Measured, not claimed. 81.5% win-probability accuracy on a true holdout: trained on 2017-2024 matches only, then scored on 2,546 matches from 2025-26 the model had never seen, rising from 79.2% at over 6 to 82.2% by over 15.

Australia vs India — FAQs

Is Australia vs India higher scoring in Australia or India?
In India. Sides batting first there average 166.0 against 160.2 in Australia, a 5.8-run difference, and 7.95 runs an over against 7.61. Across the countries we hold ground data for, Pakistan is the highest scoring at 172.4 and West Indies the lowest at 149.3.
Which ground is hardest to chase at in this fixture?
In Australia it is Sydney Cricket Ground, where sides batting first average 156.6 and chasing sides 137.6 across 93 matches — a 19.0-run gap. In India it is M Chinnaswamy Stadium, Bengaluru at 17.2. The most forgiving are Melbourne Cricket Ground (13.2) and Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad (6.8).
Who will win Australia vs India?
We do not publish pre-match tips. The model is a live model: it has nothing useful to say until a ball is bowled, and then recalculates win probability after every one from the score, wickets in hand, required rate and how the pitch is actually playing. It measures 81.5% accuracy on a true holdout — trained on 2017-2024 matches only, then scored on 2,546 matches from 2025-26 it had never seen.
Where do these numbers come from?
Ball-by-ball T20 records for the main grounds in each country — 478 matches across 6 grounds in Australia, 488 across 7 in India. They cover all T20 cricket at those venues, not internationals alone, so read them as ground character. Per-ground sample sizes are in the tables; some are small and deserve less weight.
